title: opencl-silent-abort: a self-contained reproducer for silently abandoned OpenCL kernel dispatches on Apple silicon

creators.name: Nejeoui, Abderrazzak
creators.affiliation: National School of Applied Sciences, Cadi Ayyad University, Marrakesh, Morocco

creators.name: Bekkari, Aissam
creators.affiliation: National School of Applied Sciences, Cadi Ayyad University, Marrakesh, Morocco

description:
On macOS, Apple's OpenCL runtime can report that a kernel dispatch finished successfully when the GPU never ran it. The output buffer comes back untouched, yet clEnqueueNDRangeKernel, clFinish and CL_EVENT_COMMAND_EXECUTION_STATUS all indicate success. The cause is not the kernel: macOS aborts the Metal command buffer backing the dispatch when the compute work starves the display, and Apple's OpenCL-on-Metal layer does not propagate the termination. Metal, one layer down, does report it.

This repository contains a single self-contained shell script, apple_opencl_abort_probe.sh, that reproduces and diagnoses the behaviour on any Mac in about a minute. It embeds two probe programs implementing the same kernel arithmetic over the same grid, one in OpenCL C and one in Metal Shading Language, compiles them with the system compiler, runs a load ladder, fills every output buffer with a 0xDEADBEEF sentinel so that work-items which never ran can be counted exactly, extracts the corresponding macOS unified-log entries, and prints a one-line verdict: reproduced, reproduced on the OpenCL side only, not reproduced, or not triggered. It requires no repository checkout, no network access and no credentials, and a machine that tolerates the load reports a meaningful negative result rather than a failure.

Also archived here are the machine reports collected so far, which are the complete raw output behind the measurements reported in the accompanying paper: four Apple silicon machines spanning two chip generations (M1, M1 Max, M2), three major macOS releases (14.1.1, 15.3, 26.2, 26.3.1) and GPU core counts from 8 to 32. Across them, 21 OpenCL dispatches reported CL_COMPLETE having written none of their 20000 work-items; 17 of those returned within 0.504-0.537 s (mean 0.520 s, standard deviation 0.009 s), invariant across machine, operating system and a 20x range of requested work.

An aborted dispatch is fast precisely because it did no work, so a benchmark that measures time without verifying results against a reference records its largest speedups for the runs that failed most completely. The repository is MIT-licensed so that it can be copied freely into vendor bug reports and third-party test harnesses, and it accepts contributed reports from other machines, including machines where the behaviour does not occur.
notes: Reported to Apple through Feedback Assistant as FB24808475, with the reproducer and a diagnostic report, before publication. All findings were obtained from retail machines using documented, public interfaces: no Apple binary was disassembled, decompiled or patched, no protection measure was circumvented, and no Apple code is redistributed. This is a correctness defect, not a security vulnerability. Machine reports contributed by third parties are published with their consent, with hostnames and user identifiers removed.
